intro: Occupational therapists already teach, assess and adapt daily tasks for patients. The closest of the 25 careers below is Health Specialties Teachers, Postsecondary, with a 79% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $107,310, which is 7% more than the $100,330 occupational therapists earn.
why_it_works: Your work is breaking everyday tasks into steps and coaching people to regain them. O*NET rates service orientation at 4.12 out of 5 for this job, and instructing, judgment and social perceptiveness at 4. College teaching, genetic counseling and psychology education draw on the same strengths. Few matches pay more than your current median. The gaps include problem solving with equipment and choosing the right tools.
tips: Supervise fieldwork students now; it builds the teaching record that college programs ask for.
Assistive technology work suits you if you like equipment, since equipment selection is one of your skill gaps.
Health Informatics Specialists earn $105,850 for their broader group if you want a desk role.

faq.q: What jobs can former occupational therapists do?
faq.a: The closest matches are health specialties teachers (79%), nursing instructors (78%) and Genetic Counselors (75%), based on O*NET 31.0. Genetic Counselors earn $100,040, about the same as the $100,330 occupational therapist median, so the move is about the work rather than pay.

faq.q: Which careers for occupational therapists pay more?
faq.a: Only 3 of the 25 matches pay more. Health specialties teachers earn $107,310 (7% more), earth and space sciences teachers $103,170 (3% more) and forestry and conservation science teachers $101,420 (1% more), according to BLS May 2025 data.

faq.q: Do occupational therapists need more education?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches usually need no more education than occupational therapists already have. A master's degree is common, held by 50% of workers in a close match, so your existing degree and license already cover most of these paths without new coursework.

faq.q: What skills should occupational therapists build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are complex problem solving, equipment maintenance, instructing groups and equipment selection. Judgment already rates 4 out of 5 for occupational therapists in O*NET, so the step is technical or teaching skill, not patient care.
